title: Sonal Dinusha's 1,139-Minute Marathon Denies India Series Sweep in Sri Lanka
excerpt: Sri Lankan batter scores twin centuries and bats 722 balls across the series to engineer a remarkable rearguard draw in the second Test at Colombo.
body:
• Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha scored 420 runs across four innings, spending 1,139 minutes at the crease to deny India a 2-0 series sweep.
  • Dinusha made 133 not out in the fourth innings — his third hundred in four innings — to help Sri Lanka draw the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground in Colombo.
  • He became only the third batter in Test history to score twin centuries in a match where his team was asked to follow on.
  • India won the series 1-0 but captain Shubman Gill acknowledged his side was outplayed on the final day, with the team still needing to win six of their remaining seven Tests to control their World Test Championship destiny.

A Rearguard for the Ages

Sonal Dinusha produced one of the most defiant batting performances in recent Test cricket history, spending 1,139 minutes at the crease across the two-Test series to single-handedly deny India a clean sweep in Sri Lanka.

https://x.com/ICC/status/2093300484451025223

The 25-year-old scored 420 runs across four innings — 722 balls, three centuries — and his unbeaten 133 in the final innings at Colombo's Sinhalese Sports Club Ground on August 27 ensured Sri Lanka salvaged a draw after being asked to follow on. India won the series 1-0 after taking the first Test in Galle.

Dinusha forged a critical century partnership with Keshara Nuwantha to frustrate India through the morning session on the final day. Sri Lanka had resumed just 16 runs ahead with only four wickets in hand, needing to bat out of their skin to save the match.

"In hindsight, you can say 'was the follow-on a right decision?' Keeping the weather in mind, we were not sure if there would be a full day of play on day five. Some of the things didn't go our way, but it was a brilliant game and I think test cricket won today."

— Shubman Gill, India captain

Mastering the Sweep Against India's Spinners

What made Dinusha's performance remarkable was the context in which he arrived at the crease in each innings. He walked in at 90/4 and 47/4 in the first Test, then at 122/4 and 209/4 in the second. Every time, Sri Lanka were in deep trouble.

Over 40 percent of his runs in the series came from sweeps and reverse-sweeps, according to the Times of India. India captain Gill was aware of the threat and deployed constant fielding protection on both sides of the wicket for the sweep shot. But Dinusha's smart use of footwork left the visitors clueless throughout the final day.

With no significant turn from the Colombo surface and LBW and bowled becoming unlikely dismissal modes, Dinusha feasted. He became only the third batter in Test history to score twin hundreds in a match where his team was asked to follow on — joining an elite statistical club.

Nuwantha and the Tail Provide Crucial Support

Dinusha did not bat alone. Keshara Nuwantha contributed a resilient 46, absorbing pressure during a 112-run stand that denied India through the morning session. Nuwantha survived two DRS reviews, including one in the final over before lunch when he successfully overturned an LBW decision, according to Reuters.

Spinner Manav Suthar finally broke the partnership after the interval, with his delivery catching the shoulder of Nuwantha's bat and carrying to Dhruv Jurel at slip. Jurel took a second catch to dismiss Prabath Jayasuriya for two, leaving Dinusha to bat with the tail.

Lahiru Kumara then provided invaluable support, absorbing 90 balls for a dour 12 as Sri Lanka's lower order bought time. The hosts eventually reached 429/9 when the players shook hands.

India's WTC Challenge Gets Tougher

For India, the drawn match was a missed opportunity. Currently fifth in the World Test Championship standings, Gill's side now faces a steep path to the final. They travel to New Zealand for two Tests later this year before hosting Australia in a blockbuster five-match series early in 2027.

"If we have a good New Zealand series, and as long as we have a chance, we'll keep believing. Hopefully we'll make it to the WTC final," Gill said at the post-match presentation.

India must win at least six of their remaining seven Tests to control their destiny in the championship race.

Looking Ahead

Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva praised the performances of Dinusha, Pasindu Sooriyabandara, and all-rounder Nuwantha. For Dinusha, the series establishes him as one of Asian cricket's most exciting young talents — a player who made time his closest ally and rewrote the record books in the process.
